text: Git branches let developers work on features in isolation from the main codebase. The default branch is usually called main or master.
A pull request proposes changes from one branch to another and allows reviewers to comment before merging.
Git rebase rewrites commit history by moving a branch onto a new base commit, producing a linear history.
Git merge combines two branches by creating a new merge commit that has two parents.
A merge conflict happens when the same lines of a file are changed differently in two branches being merged.
git stash temporarily shelves uncommitted changes so you can work on something else, then reapplies them later with git stash pop.
A fork is a personal copy of someone else's repository that lives in your own GitHub account.
git clone downloads a full copy of a remote repository, including its entire commit history, to your local machine.
The .gitignore file lists patterns for files and directories that Git should not track, such as build artifacts or secrets.
git bisect performs a binary search through commit history to find the commit that introduced a bug.
A commit hash is a SHA-1 checksum that uniquely identifies a specific snapshot of the repository.
git revert creates a new commit that undoes the changes of a previous commit, without rewriting history.
git reset moves the current branch pointer to a different commit, optionally changing the working directory and staging area.
A detached HEAD state occurs when you check out a specific commit instead of a branch, so new commits won't belong to any branch.
Continuous integration automatically builds and tests code every time changes are pushed, catching problems early.
A code owner file specifies which individuals or teams are automatically requested for review on changes to certain files.
Semantic versioning uses a MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH format where MAJOR changes break compatibility, MINOR adds features, and PATCH fixes bugs.
A changelog is a file that records notable changes made to a project in each released version.
An issue tracker lets users report bugs and request features, and lets maintainers triage and prioritize work.
A GitHub Action is an automated workflow defined in YAML that runs in response to repository events like pushes or pull requests.
Squashing commits combines multiple commits into a single commit, often used to clean up history before merging.
A tag marks a specific commit, commonly used to mark release points such as v1.0.0.
An upstream repository is the original repository that a fork was created from.
git fetch downloads new data from a remote repository without merging it into your local branches, unlike git pull.
A README file is the first document most people see when visiting a repository, usually describing what the project does and how to use it.
